sections.title: Overview

summary.text: Gives an overview of the technical brief, which updates WHO guidance to support differentiated, simplified, demedicalized PrEP services in line with the 2022–2030 global health sector strategies. It lists key points on starting and stopping oral PrEP, including event-driven dosing for people assigned male at birth not taking estradiol-based hormones, and on hepatitis B and C testing. It also introduces the four building blocks of differentiated delivery: where, who, when and what.

sections.extract: What is this technical brief? This technical brief by the World Health Organization (WHO) updates and supplements previous WHO guidelines and guidance on pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) for HIV prevention. The brief aims to support differentiated, simplified, demedicalized and comprehensive PrEP services. This can support PrEP uptake, persistence and effective use and assist efforts to achieve global goals set out

sections.title: Background

summary.text: Explains what PrEP is and recalls that WHO's 2015 recommendation of TDF-based oral PrEP was cautious because experience was limited, whereas services have since been widely simplified, demedicalized and integrated. It states the brief's aim of supporting these trends, accelerated by COVID-19, towards the UN target of fewer than 370 000 new infections by 2025, and summarises WHO PrEP recommendations in a box.

sections.extract: Pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) for HIV prevention is the use of antiretroviral drugs by HIV-negative individuals to reduce the risk of acquisition of HIV. The World Health Organization (WHO) has recommended multiple PrEP options as part of combination prevention approaches (Box 1). When WHO recommended offering TDF-based oral PrEP to people at substantial risk for HIV in 2015 (Box 2), implementation of PrEP

sections.title: Target audience and scope

summary.text: Describes the brief's audience and scope: it supplements WHO consolidated HIV guidelines and the PrEP Implementation Tool, focusing on TDF-based oral PrEP while noting considerations for the dapivirine vaginal ring and long-acting cabotegravir.

sections.extract: This technical brief aims to support a range of stakeholders in planning and implementing PrEP services. It provides guidance on PrEP implementation and is meant to supplement and update guidance previously published in the WHO Consolidated HIV Guidelines (4) and the WHO PrEP Implementation Tool.3 The guidance in this document relates primarily to TDF-based oral PrEP (including TDF in combination with emtricitabine

sections.title: Guiding principle and methodology

summary.text: Describes the brief's people-centred, rights-based approach and how it was developed by a WHO core group with an expert working group, including management of declarations of interest. It also begins guidance that eligible people assigned male at birth may choose event-driven or daily oral PrEP, with a footnote defining transgender people.

sections.extract: This technical brief follows a public health, human rights and people-centred approach to provide evidence-based guidance on PrEP service delivery. Such an approach puts the people and communities who could benefit from PrEP services at the centre of service delivery, adapting services to their preferences and needs while maximizing impact and health system efficiency. The development of this brief was led by a core

sections.title: Starting and stopping oral PrEP

summary.text: Sets out how to start and stop oral PrEP: people eligible for event-driven PrEP take a double loading dose 2–24 hours before sex and continue daily until two days after the last exposure. All other groups, including cisgender women and people who inject drugs, take seven daily doses before protection and stop seven days after the last exposure. A figure illustrates the dosing timelines.

sections.extract: To reduce the risk of HIV acquisition through sexual exposure, cisgender men and trans and gender diverse people assigned male at birth4 who are not taking exogenous estradiol-based hormones may be offered oral daily PrEP or ED-PrEP as options (Table 1 and Figure 1). Whether the intention is to use oral daily PrEP or ED-PrEP, people eligible for ED-PrEP can start and stop PrEP using the same strategy: • Start PrEP

sections.title: Rationale

summary.text: Explains the evidence that event-driven PrEP is as effective as daily PrEP for cisgender men who have sex with men and why it can be extended to all people assigned male at birth not taking estradiol-based hormones, regardless of sexual positioning. It notes insufficient evidence for other groups and compares lead-in and stopping times recommended in other guidelines.

sections.extract: Data from trials, open label extension studies and demonstration studies have shown that oral PrEP using the ED-PrEP dosing regimen is as effective in preventing HIV infection as daily PrEP in cisgender men who have sex with men (6–8). As a result, WHO recommended that an ED-PrEP regimen is safe and highly effective in reducing risk of HIV acquisition through receptive and/ or insertive sex between cisgender men and

sections.title: PrEP and hepatitis B and C

summary.text: Gives a flowchart-style summary of hepatitis B management in PrEP services: vaccination for those testing HBsAg-negative and assessment for treatment for those positive. It explains that TDF-based PrEP also suppresses hepatitis B, notes the small risk of relapse after stopping and the need for monitoring.

sections.title: Hepatitis B virus

summary.text: Recommends testing PrEP users once for hepatitis B surface antigen, especially in highly endemic countries, while stressing that lack of testing must not delay PrEP. It notes that oral PrEP and the dapivirine ring are safe for people with hepatitis B or C and repeats the key points on hepatitis testing.

sections.extract: Testing PrEP users for HBsAg once, at or within one to three months of PrEP initiation (or later if not available around initiation), is strongly encouraged, particularly in highly endemic countries. TDF-based daily or event- driven oral PrEP and the DVR can be safely offered to persons with HBV infection. There are specific considerations regarding offering CAB-LA to people with HBV (Box 3). HBV testing is not a

sections.title: Hepatitis C virus

summary.text: Recommends hepatitis C antibody testing at PrEP start and yearly for populations at high risk, while making clear that testing is not a requirement for PrEP. It covers referral for treatment, HCV self-testing and specific considerations for long-acting cabotegravir in people with hepatitis C.

sections.extract: HCV antibody testing is strongly encouraged at or within one to three months of PrEP initiation (or later if not available around initiation), and every 12 months thereafter, where PrEP services are provided to populations at high risk of HCV infection. Risks of HCV vary across settings, and populations at high risk of HCV include, but are not limited to, cisgender men and transgender women who have sex with men,

sections.title: Rationale

summary.text: Explains the rationale for the hepatitis guidance, citing global estimates of hepatitis B and C burden and the 2030 elimination goal. It revises earlier advice by stating that hepatitis B infection does not rule out event-driven PrEP, because clinical relapse is rare, and discusses PrEP choices for pregnant people living with hepatitis B.

sections.extract: WHO estimates that in 2019, there were 296 million people living with chronic HBV infection and 58 million people living with HCV infection worldwide (31). An estimated 1.1 million deaths in 2019 were due to HBV and HCV infection. The Global Health Sector Strategy on Viral Hepatitis, approved by the World Health Assembly in 2016, set the goal to eliminate viral hepatitis as a major public health threat by 2030 (32).

sections.title: PrEP and kidney function

summary.text: Sets out guidance on kidney function and TDF-based oral PrEP: impaired kidney function is a contraindication, but testing is optional for people under 30 without comorbidities and can be limited for others. It advises that waiting for results should not delay PrEP and that tests be repeated before stopping. Notes cover estimating kidney function, including during pregnancy and gender-affirming hormone use.

sections.extract: Impaired kidney function, indicated by an eGFR of <60 mL/min per 1.73 m2 or an estimated creatinine clearance of <60 mL/min, is a contraindication for the use of TDF-based oral PrEP. Measuring kidney function in potential PrEP users at initiation and during PrEP continuation is suggested for some populations. Table 2 outlines suggested procedures (applicable to oral daily PrEP or ED-PrEP). Box 4 provides suggestions

sections.title: Rationale

summary.text: Explains the rationale for reduced kidney testing, citing meta-analyses showing mostly mild, reversible kidney effects and data from over 18 000 people screened in which abnormal values were rare and increased with age.

sections.extract: Multiple systematic reviews and meta-analyses of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) found that individuals taking TDF-based oral PrEP have, on average, a higher risk of experiencing kidney-related adverse events compared with individuals taking placebos (46–48), but these adverse events tend to be mild, nonprogressive, and reversible after PrEP discontinuation. sections.extract: (HIVST) for PrEP

sections.title: HIVST and PrEP

summary.text: Describes how HIV self-testing can support PrEP, drawing on COVID-19 experience and a review showing fewer clinic visits and testing between visits. It outlines three uses—demand generation and linkage, PrEP initiation, and continuation—and notes the need for community engagement and further operational research.

sections.extract: HIVST could be an important tool to enable countries to increase access to PrEP and uptake, persistence and effective use. Since the beginning of the COVID-19 pandemic, WHO has supported HIVST to maintain PrEP services (51), and several countries have integrated HIVST into their PrEP programming to initiate and continue clients on PrEP (see Box 6 and 10 in next section). A literature review found evidence that HIVST

sections.title: What is HIVST?

summary.text: Explains what HIV self-testing is, its WHO recommendation since 2016 and the prequalified products available. It discusses using self-testing to start PrEP outside clinics despite limited evidence, addressing concerns about acute infection and drug resistance. Modelling summarised here suggests that self-testing may miss some infections but that drug-resistance prevalence stays similar across scenarios.

sections.extract: In HIVST, people collect their own specimen (generally oral fluid or fingerprick whole blood) using a simple rapid HIV test and then perform the test and interpret their result, often in private or with someone they trust. WHO has recommended HIVST as an approach to HIV testing services since 2016 (4), and the approach has been scaled up globally with nearly 100 countries reporting national policies.6 Currently,

sections.title: Rationale

summary.text: Summarises a systematic review of self-testing for PrEP, including a Kenyan trial in which six-month dispensing with self-testing halved clinic visits without reducing persistence.

sections.extract: A systematic review on HIVST for PrEP initiation and continuation (52) identified three completed RCTs that evaluated PrEP continuation after initiation in health care facilities, while no studies evaluated HIVST-based PrEP initiation. All studies evaluated oral PrEP. An RCT in Kenya that evaluated six-month PrEP dispensing supported with HIVST between clinic visits found that PrEP clinic visits were halved, while

sections.title: Building blocks of differentiated PrEP service delivery

summary.text: Introduces differentiated PrEP delivery, noting the shift away from clinic-only physician prescribing that accelerated during COVID-19.

sections.extract: delivery In many countries, individuals interested in PrEP must go to a health care facility (often an HIV clinic) to obtain a prescription from a medical provider (often a physician). In recent years, and particularly during the COVID-19 pandemic (60), the shift towards differentiated PrEP service delivery has accelerated.

sections.title: Differentiated PrEP service delivery: When, where, who and what to deliver

summary.text: Defines differentiated PrEP service delivery as person- and community-centred and links it to the global health sector strategies. It presents the four building blocks (when, where, who and what), which can differ between initiation, continuation and re-initiation and across PrEP products.

sections.extract: delivery: When, where, who and what to deliver A differentiated PrEP service delivery approach is person- and community-centred and adapts services to the needs and preferences of the people who are interested in and could benefit from PrEP. Differentiated PrEP service delivery may also support more efficient and cost–effective use of health care resources. WHO recommends differentiated service delivery for HIV

sections.title: Where to deliver PrEP

summary.text: Sets out barriers to PrEP in health facilities, such as stigma, lack of privacy, distance, costs and long waits, as well as provider-side barriers. It argues that oral PrEP and the ring have few required components and can be delivered in community settings, while more research is needed for long-acting cabotegravir. Evidence and provider views on community-based delivery follow.

sections.extract: There are a range of barriers to PrEP access, uptake, persistence and effective use associated with service delivery in health care facilities. These include actual or perceived lack of privacy, stigma and discrimination, negative attitudes of health care providers, travel distance, direct and opportunity costs for clients, frequency of required clinic visits for continuation, lengthy waiting times and inconvenient

sections.title: PrEP in fixed and mobile community settings

summary.text: Describes oral PrEP delivery in fixed and mobile community sites, such as NGO centres and vans, and the importance of partnerships with community organizations and integrated services. A box summarises review evidence, including the SEARCH trial in Kenya and Uganda and the Love O2O study in Thailand, and an example from Viet Nam is pictured.

sections.extract: Service models that deliver oral PrEP in fixed community sites (such as through nongovernmental organizations) and mobile and semimobile sites (for example, vans parked in community settings) have been implemented. A systematic review (Box 7) (63) identified diverse models demonstrating the feasibility of these approaches in a range of countries, but data on effectiveness were limited. In addition to considerations

sections.title: Telehealth for PrEP

summary.text: Describes telehealth platforms for delivering PrEP, which WHO supports as an additional option provided data security and confidentiality are protected. It lists aspects of service delivery that telehealth can support, such as risk assessment, home delivery of self-test kits and prescriptions. Evidence from case studies and ongoing US trials is summarised, with a photo from a Brazilian project.

sections.extract: The use of information and telecommunication technologies to create virtual platforms for delivering PrEP services has the potential to remove barriers to PrEP uptake and persistence and support effective use of PrEP. WHO recommends that online delivery of HIV, viral hepatitis and STI services to key populations may be offered as an additional option, while ensuring that data security and confidentiality are

sections.title: PrEP delivery in pharmacies

summary.text: Explains that pharmacies can be more accessible and convenient than clinics and may expand PrEP access, though effectiveness and cost-effectiveness of pharmacy delivery remain unknown. It sets out what pharmacists need, such as legal authority, testing infrastructure and training, and cites Kenyan experience showing similar uptake and persistence, noting that legal changes are needed for pharmacists to prescribe PrEP.

sections.extract: Pharmacies can be more accessible, acceptable and convenient for clients than health care facilities. In resource-limited settings, individuals commonly first seek health care services from pharmacies before going to clinics (72,73). The WHO Guideline on Self- Care Interventions for Health and Well-Being (74) notes that providing PrEP through pharmacies may present an opportunity to expand access to PrEP. However,

sections.title: Who to deliver PrEP

summary.text: Contrasts WHO task-sharing recommendations for ART with PrEP, which in most countries is prescribed by clinicians while lay providers handle other tasks such as risk assessment and HIV testing. It argues that sharing PrEP tasks with peers and community health workers may improve efficiency and acceptability, noting research needs for long-acting cabotegravir and requirements for training, quality assurance, clinical oversight and fair pay.

sections.extract: For HIV treatment, WHO recommends (4) that 1) trained nonphysician clinicians, nurses and midwives can initiate and maintain ART, and 2) trained and supervised community health workers can dispense ART and lay providers can distribute ART. For PrEP, in most countries a clinician prescribes PrEP, while other health care providers (for example, lay providers) may deliver other aspects of PrEP services, such as

sections.title: When and what services to deliver

summary.text: Discusses when and what PrEP services to deliver, starting with multi-month dispensing, which is standard for ART and is being adapted for PrEP after an initial one-month visit, with examples from Viet Nam, Zimbabwe and a Kenyan trial of six-month dispensing with HIV self-testing. It then covers integrating PrEP with other services, such as gender-affirming care, harm reduction, antenatal and family planning services, and a status-neutral approach to testing. It ends with a case study from Glasgow on PrEP for people who inject drugs, where staffing intensity limits expansion.

sections.extract: Multi-month dispensing (MMD) WHO recommends that people living with HIV established on ART should be offered three-to-six– month ART refills, preferably lasting six months (4). MMD of ART has been found to be feasible and cost- saving for providers and clients in a range of countries, and COVID-19 has accelerated adoption of ART MMD (83). For oral PrEP, a one-month supply is commonly provided at initiation,

sections.title: Research gaps

summary.text: Identifies research gaps for differentiated PrEP delivery, calling for implementation science and quasi-experimental methods to measure effects on uptake, persistence and effective use. It notes that evidence is concentrated among men who have sex with men and young women in a few countries, and that experience with the dapivirine ring and long-acting cabotegravir is still lacking.

sections.extract: While the feasibility of a range of differentiated PrEP service delivery models has been demonstrated, additional evidence of effectiveness of PrEP-related outcomes (uptake, persistence and effective use) is needed. Implementation science and quasi- experimental approaches, such as difference-in- differences methods for pre–post evaluations of interventions, could provide robust evidence on effectiveness,

sections.title: Annex 1: Summary of mathematical modelling of HIVST for PrEP in Kenya

summary.text: Annex 1, summarizing mathematical modelling of HIV self-testing for community-based oral PrEP delivery in Kenya. It concludes that expanding PrEP could avert nearly half of new infections over 20 years and that self-testing-based delivery could be effective, with only small increases in inappropriate PrEP use and drug resistance compared with provider testing.

sections.title: Annex 2: Background and methods on the global PrEP provider study

summary.text: Annex 2, describing the methods of a WHO-supported global survey and in-depth interviews of PrEP providers carried out between November 2021 and February 2022 on service practices and views of new PrEP products. It explains how questions were developed and translated and lists participating providers by WHO region and country.

sections.extract: methods on the global PrEP provider study WHO supported a global study of PrEP providers, comprising an online survey and in-depth interviews, from November 2021 through February 2022. The survey aimed to understand current service delivery practices as well as perspectives on new PrEP products. Follow-up interviews with survey participants were conducted to gain additional insights and to offer an opportunity for

sections.title: Annex 3: Summary of a review of PrEP services for people who inject drugs

summary.text: Annex 3, summarizing a review of PrEP services for people who inject drugs, which found limited availability and use. It recommends expanding PrEP within harm reduction programmes, preferably community-based and peer-led, and lists service models found, before ending with WHO's contact details.

narratives.en: Page render with the end of Table 1 and Figure 1. The table gives oral PrEP dosing by population: cisgender men and trans and gender diverse people assigned male at birth with sexual exposure who are not taking exogenous estradiol-based hormones take a double dose 2–24 hours before exposure, one dose per day, and one dose per day until two days after the last exposure; other populations (including cisgender women, people taking estradiol-based hormones and people preventing HIV acquisition from injecting practices) take one dose daily for seven days before exposure, one dose per day, and one dose daily for seven days after the last exposure. Figure 1 shows day-by-day timelines with pill icons: for those eligible for ED-PrEP, a double dose then daily doses through two days after sex (within or beyond 24 hours of the initial dose); for those not eligible, seven daily doses before exposure, continued daily dosing, and seven daily doses after the last exposure.
narratives.ar: عرض لصفحة يتضمن نهاية الجدول 1 والشكل 1. يعرض الجدول جرعات الوقاية الفموية قبل التعرض (PrEP) حسب الفئة السكانية: الرجال المتوافقو الجنس والأشخاص العابرون جنسياً والمتنوعون جنسانياً المحددون ذكوراً عند الولادة الذين يتعرضون جنسياً ولا يتناولون هرمونات خارجية قائمة على الإستراديول يتناولون جرعة مضاعفة قبل التعرض بـ 2–24 ساعة، ثم جرعة واحدة يومياً، ثم جرعة يومياً حتى يومين بعد آخر تعرض؛ أما الفئات الأخرى (بما فيها النساء المتوافقات الجنس ومن يتناولون هرمونات قائمة على الإستراديول ومن يقون أنفسهم من اكتساب الفيروس عبر ممارسات الحقن) فتتناول جرعة يومياً لمدة سبعة أيام قبل التعرض، ثم جرعة يومياً، ثم جرعة يومياً لمدة سبعة أيام بعد آخر تعرض. ويعرض الشكل 1 جداول زمنية يوماً بيوم مع أيقونات أقراص: للمؤهلين للوقاية المرتبطة بالحدث (ED-PrEP)، جرعة مضاعفة ثم جرعات يومية حتى يومين بعد الجماع (خلال 24 ساعة من الجرعة الأولى أو بعدها)؛ ولغير المؤهلين، سبع جرعات يومية قبل التعرض، ثم الاستمرار يومياً، ثم سبع جرعات يومية بعد آخر تعرض.
narratives.zh: 页面渲染图，包含表1结尾和图1。表格按人群列出口服暴露前预防（PrEP）的用药方法：有性暴露且未使用外源性雌二醇类激素的顺性别男性及出生时被指定为男性的跨性别和性别多元者，在潜在暴露前2–24小时服用双倍剂量，此后每天一剂，并每天一剂直至最后一次暴露后两天；其他人群（包括顺性别女性、使用雌二醇类激素者以及为预防注射行为感染艾滋病毒而使用PrEP者）在潜在暴露前连续七天每天一剂，此后每天一剂，并在最后一次暴露后连续七天每天一剂。图1以药片图标逐日展示时间线：符合事件驱动PrEP（ED-PrEP）条件者先服双倍剂量，然后每天服药直至性行为后两天（性行为在首次剂量后24小时内或超过24小时）；不符合条件者在暴露前每天服药七天，持续每天服药，并在最后一次暴露后每天服药七天。
narratives.es: Imagen de página con el final del cuadro 1 y la figura 1. El cuadro indica la posología de la PrEP oral por población: los hombres cisgénero y las personas trans y de género diverso a las que se asignó el sexo masculino al nacer, con exposición sexual y que no toman hormonas exógenas a base de estradiol, toman una dosis doble entre 2 y 24 horas antes de la exposición, una dosis al día y una dosis al día hasta dos días después de la última exposición; las demás poblaciones (incluidas las mujeres cisgénero, las personas que toman hormonas a base de estradiol y las personas que usan la PrEP para prevenir la infección por el VIH asociada a prácticas de inyección) toman una dosis diaria durante siete días antes de la exposición, una dosis al día y una dosis diaria durante siete días después de la última exposición. La figura 1 muestra cronologías día a día con iconos de comprimidos: para las personas idóneas para la PrEP a demanda (ED-PrEP), una dosis doble y luego dosis diarias hasta dos días después de la relación sexual (dentro o más allá de las 24 horas siguientes a la dosis inicial); para las no idóneas, siete dosis diarias antes de la exposición, dosis diarias continuas y siete dosis diarias tras la última exposición.
narratives.fr: Rendu de page comprenant la fin du tableau 1 et la figure 1. Le tableau indique la posologie de la PrEP orale par population : les hommes cisgenres et les personnes trans et de genre divers assignées au sexe masculin à la naissance ayant une exposition sexuelle et ne prenant pas d’hormones exogènes à base d’estradiol prennent une double dose 2 à 24 heures avant l’exposition, une dose par jour, et une dose par jour jusqu’à deux jours après la dernière exposition ; les autres populations (dont les femmes cisgenres, les personnes prenant des hormones à base d’estradiol et les personnes utilisant la PrEP pour prévenir l’acquisition du VIH liée aux pratiques d’injection) prennent une dose quotidienne pendant sept jours avant l’exposition, une dose par jour, et une dose quotidienne pendant sept jours après la dernière exposition. La figure 1 présente des chronologies jour par jour avec des icônes de comprimés : pour les personnes éligibles à la PrEP à la demande (ED-PrEP), une double dose puis des doses quotidiennes jusqu’à deux jours après le rapport (dans les 24 heures suivant la dose initiale ou au-delà) ; pour les personnes non éligibles, sept doses quotidiennes avant l’exposition, la poursuite des doses quotidiennes et sept doses quotidiennes après la dernière exposition.
narratives.ru: Изображение страницы с окончанием таблицы 1 и рисунком 1. В таблице приведена схема приема пероральной ДКП по группам населения: цисгендерные мужчины и трансгендерные и гендерно разнообразные люди, которым при рождении был приписан мужской пол, имеющие половые контакты и не принимающие экзогенные гормоны на основе эстрадиола, принимают двойную дозу за 2–24 часа до контакта, затем одну дозу в день и одну дозу в день до двух дней после последнего контакта; другие группы (включая цисгендерных женщин, людей, принимающих гормоны на основе эстрадиола, и людей, использующих ДКП для профилактики заражения ВИЧ при инъекционных практиках) принимают одну дозу ежедневно в течение семи дней до контакта, затем одну дозу в день и одну дозу ежедневно в течение семи дней после последнего контакта. На рисунке 1 показаны пошаговые графики по дням со значками таблеток: для лиц, которым подходит ДКП по требованию (ED-PrEP), — двойная доза, затем ежедневные дозы до двух дней после полового контакта (в пределах 24 часов после первой дозы или позже); для остальных — семь ежедневных доз до контакта, продолжение ежедневного приема и семь ежедневных доз после последнего контакта.

tables.caption: Table 1. Starting, using and stopping TDF-based oral PrEP safely
rows: Cisgender men and trans and gender diverse people assigned male at birtha who: • have sexual exposure AND • are not taking exogenous estradiol-based hormones
Take a double dose 2–24 hours before potential sexual exposure (ideally closer to 24 hours before potential exposure)
Take one dose per day
Take one dose per day until two days after the day of the last potential sexual exposure

Cisgender women and trans and gender diverse people assigned female at birtha Cisgender men and trans and gender diverse people assigned male at birtha who are taking exogenous estradiol-based hormones People using oral PrEP to prevent HIV acquisition from injecting practices
Take one dose daily for seven days before potential exposure
Take one dose per day
Take one dose daily for seven days after last potential exposure
tables.notes: PrEP: pre-exposure prophylaxis; TDF: tenofovir disoproxil fumarate. a “Trans and gender diverse people” is an umbrella term for those whose gender identity, roles and expression does not conform to the norms and expectations traditionally associated with the sex assigned to them at birth; it includes people who are transsexual, transgender, or otherwise gender nonconforming or gender incongruent. Transgender people may self-identify as transgender, female, male, transwoman or transman, trans-sexual or one of many other gender nonconforming identities. [Row 2 groups three populations (printed as separate paragraphs in one cell) that share the same regimen.]

narratives.en: How to start, use and stop TDF-based oral PrEP for two groups: people assigned male at birth with sexual exposure who are not taking estradiol-based hormones (eligible for a double starting dose), and all other populations, including people assigned female at birth, those taking estradiol-based hormones and people who inject drugs (seven-day lead-in and stopping periods).
narratives.ar: كيفية بدء العلاج الوقائي قبل التعرض الفموي القائم على TDF واستخدامه وإيقافه لمجموعتين: الأشخاص المحدد جنسهم عند الولادة ذكوراً المعرضون جنسياً ولا يتناولون هرمونات قائمة على الإستراديول (يحق لهم بدء العلاج بجرعة مضاعفة)، وسائر الفئات الأخرى، بمن فيها الأشخاص المحدد جنسهم عند الولادة إناثاً ومن يتناولون هرمونات الإستراديول ومتعاطو المخدرات بالحقن (فترة بدء وإيقاف مدتها سبعة أيام).
narratives.zh: 针对两类人群说明如何开始、使用和停止以TDF为基础的口服暴露前预防：出生时被指定为男性、有性暴露且未服用雌二醇类激素者（可采用双倍起始剂量），以及所有其他人群，包括出生时被指定为女性者、服用雌二醇类激素者和注射吸毒者（开始前和停止后各需七天）。
narratives.es: Cómo iniciar, usar y suspender la PrEP oral basada en TDF para dos grupos: personas a las que se asignó el sexo masculino al nacer con exposición sexual que no toman hormonas a base de estradiol (aptas para una dosis doble inicial) y todas las demás poblaciones, incluidas las personas a las que se asignó el sexo femenino al nacer, las que toman hormonas a base de estradiol y las personas que se inyectan drogas (siete días antes y después).
narratives.fr: Comment commencer, utiliser et arrêter la PrEP orale à base de TDF pour deux groupes : les personnes de sexe masculin assigné à la naissance ayant une exposition sexuelle et ne prenant pas d’hormones à base d’estradiol (éligibles à une double dose initiale), et toutes les autres populations, y compris les personnes de sexe féminin assigné à la naissance, celles prenant des hormones à base d’estradiol et les personnes qui s’injectent des drogues (sept jours avant et après).
narratives.ru: Порядок начала, применения и прекращения пероральной ДКП на основе TDF для двух групп: лиц, которым при рождении был присвоен мужской пол, имеющих половой контакт и не принимающих препараты на основе эстрадиола (может применяться двойная начальная доза), и всех остальных групп, включая лиц, которым при рождении был присвоен женский пол, принимающих эстрадиол и потребителей инъекционных наркотиков (по семь дней до и после).

tables.notes: eGFR: estimated glomerular filtration rate; PrEP: pre-exposure prophylaxis; TDF: tenofovir disoproxil fumarate. a Kidney-related comorbidities include chronic kidney disease or risk factors such as diabetes or hypertension. There may be an increased risk of kidney-related adverse events during pregnancy, and conditions such as preeclampsia may cause kidney impairment, so more frequent kidney function testing may be considered during pregnancy. b eGFR ≥90 mL/min per 1.73 m2 or creatinine clearance of ≥90 mL/min. c eGFR <90 mL/min per 1.73 m2 or creatinine clearance of <90 mL/min. d Risks of kidney impairment and kidney-related adverse events remain low among those aged 30–49 years without kidney-related comorbidities, particularly those aged 30–39, so kidney function monitoring can be considered optional in this group, too, depending on available resources.

narratives.en: Suggested kidney function testing at PrEP initiation and at follow-up for people taking TDF-containing oral PrEP, by population group defined by age (under 30, 30–49, 50+), kidney-related comorbidities and previous evidence of reduced kidney function.
narratives.ar: الإجراءات المقترحة لفحص وظائف الكلى عند بدء العلاج الوقائي قبل التعرض وخلال المتابعة لمن يتناولون العلاج الفموي المحتوي على TDF، بحسب الفئة السكانية المحددة بالعمر (دون 30، و30–49، و50 فأكثر) والأمراض المصاحبة المتعلقة بالكلى والأدلة السابقة على تراجع وظائف الكلى.
narratives.zh: 针对服用含TDF口服暴露前预防药物者，按年龄（30岁以下、30–49岁、50岁及以上）、肾脏相关合并症及既往肾功能下降证据划分人群，建议在开始用药时和随访时进行的肾功能检测。
narratives.es: Pruebas de función renal sugeridas al inicio de la PrEP y durante el seguimiento en personas que toman PrEP oral con TDF, por grupo de población según la edad (menos de 30, 30-49, 50 o más), las comorbilidades renales y los antecedentes de disminución de la función renal.
narratives.fr: Examens de la fonction rénale suggérés à l’instauration de la PrEP et pendant le suivi chez les personnes prenant une PrEP orale contenant du TDF, par groupe de population défini selon l’âge (moins de 30 ans, 30-49 ans, 50 ans et plus), les comorbidités rénales et des antécédents de diminution de la fonction rénale.
narratives.ru: Рекомендуемое исследование функции почек при начале ДКП и в ходе последующего наблюдения у лиц, принимающих пероральную ДКП с TDF, по группам населения в зависимости от возраста (до 30, 30–49, 50+ лет), сопутствующих заболеваний почек и ранее выявленного снижения функции почек.

narratives.en: Framework for differentiated PrEP service delivery: for each building block (where, who, when, what), the table names what has to be defined at initiation, initial follow-up and re-initiation, and during continuation (PrEP refills and follow-up).
narratives.ar: إطار لتقديم خدمات متمايزة للعلاج الوقائي قبل التعرض: لكل لبنة أساسية (أين، ومن، ومتى، وماذا) يحدد الجدول ما ينبغي تحديده عند البدء والمتابعة الأولية وإعادة البدء، وخلال الاستمرار (إعادة صرف الدواء والمتابعة).
narratives.zh: 差异化暴露前预防服务提供框架：针对每个基本要素（在哪里、由谁、何时、提供什么），该表列出在开始用药、初始随访和重新开始阶段以及持续用药阶段（续药和随访）需要确定的内容。
narratives.es: Marco para la prestación diferenciada de servicios de PrEP: para cada componente básico (dónde, quién, cuándo, qué), el cuadro indica lo que debe definirse al inicio, en el seguimiento inicial y al reiniciar, y durante la continuación (reposición de la PrEP y seguimiento).
narratives.fr: Cadre de prestation différenciée des services de PrEP : pour chaque élément constitutif (où, qui, quand, quoi), le tableau indique ce qui doit être défini à l’instauration, lors du suivi initial et de la reprise, et pendant la poursuite (renouvellement de la PrEP et suivi).
narratives.ru: Схема дифференцированного предоставления услуг ДКП: для каждого структурного элемента (где, кто, когда, что) в таблице указано, что необходимо определить при начале, первичном наблюдении и возобновлении приема, а также на этапе продолжения (пополнение запаса ДКП и последующее наблюдение).
